classification.rationale: Human dietary tracer appearance and source-specific postprandial kinetics are physiological propositions requiring appraisal.
classification.intervention: Existing amino-acid supply relationships remain unchanged.
classification.exact_proposition: Dietary protein supplies phenylalanine to the human circulation, with delivery kinetics varying by the tested protein source, dose and meal context. The pooled age association is context-dependent, not proof that ageing uniformly impairs absorption or that greater availability increases brain neurotransmitters.

classification.rationale: Whole-diet adequacy and protein-quality synthesis is not a molecular identity. An incomplete appraisal must not be relabelled as foundational biology.
classification.intervention: Whole-diet adequacy is distinct from requiring every meal to contain an identical complete set; no admission changed.
classification.exact_proposition: Varied adult diets can provide digestible indispensable amino acids without requiring every meal to supply the full set. This nutritional-adequacy proposition does not establish an optimal neurotransmitter dose or demonstrate that all plant and animal foods have identical postprandial responses.

classification.classification: Mixed proposition: retain active Finding; isolate pure PAH reaction as PM1-SP1
classification.rationale: The exact historical statement includes a physiological contribution to tyrosine supply. It is broader than reaction identity; reclassifying the whole record would hide an appraisal question. The active descriptive title now states the physiological scope.
classification.SEC: Existing non-numerical snapshot unchanged; classification note explains applicability. No new factors or score.
classification.intervention: Derived precursor supply remains unchanged; reaction identity alone does not establish quantitative dietary contribution or brain flux.
classification.exact_proposition: Phenylalanine-4-hydroxylase (PAH) converts L-phenylalanine to L-tyrosine. This endogenous route contributes to tyrosine supply but does not make tyrosine absent from foods or establish an independent requirement for extra dietary tyrosine.

classification.classification: Scientific Principle PM1-SP2; original Finding preserved as historical
classification.rationale: Precursor identities are foundational pathway membership. The dietary-effect cautions remain scope limitations rather than newly established negative intervention results.
classification.SEC: Not applicable to the active Principle. The original F4 assessment and previous versions remain available through the audit renderer.
classification.intervention: No intervention efficacy follows from identifying the precursors.
classification.exact_proposition: Tyrosine and tryptophan supply the precursor pathways for catecholamines and serotonin, respectively. Their biochemical identity does not demonstrate that additional meal protein improves brain transmitter synthesis, attention, mood or reward.

classification.rationale: Food texture affected measured tracer appearance under a defined experimental protocol, with endpoint-specific null results.
classification.intervention: Existing stored PM1-SOP-DEFERRED-1 relationship remains unchanged. Older prose still calls it proposed/absent; this pre-existing mismatch is flagged for review, not resolved by changing admission.
classification.exact_proposition: In a randomised crossover study of ten older men, 135 g minced beef produced greater six-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance than the same quantity of steak. Total plasma essential-amino-acid concentrations and muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably between preparations.

classification.rationale: Formulation-specific early kinetics and integrated-exposure null results require appraisal; processing effects are not foundational reaction identities.
classification.intervention: No extrusion-related SOP is admitted by this pilot.
classification.exact_proposition: In a randomised crossover of nine healthy young adults, the tested high-moisture-extruded mycoprotein/pea blend delayed selected early plasma amino-acid responses relative to the dry blend. Total five-hour grouped amino-acid availability was not significantly different; the study does not establish poorer overall nutrition for all meat alternatives.

principles.title: Phenylalanine hydroxylase reaction
principles.proposition: Phenylalanine-4-hydroxylase catalyses conversion of L-phenylalanine to L-tyrosine.
principles.scope_limitations: Reaction identity does not quantify physiological conversion flux, dietary contribution to tyrosine supply or brain catecholamine synthesis. Those propositions remain subject to scientific appraisal in SF3.
principles.classification_rationale: Only the established reaction identity is a Principle; the original mixed physiological proposition remains an active Finding.

principles.historical_proposition: Tyrosine and tryptophan supply the precursor pathways for catecholamines and serotonin, respectively. Their biochemical identity does not demonstrate that additional meal protein improves brain transmitter synthesis, attention, mood or reward.
principles.title: Tyrosine and tryptophan precursor identities
principles.proposition: Tyrosine is a precursor in catecholamine biosynthesis; tryptophan is a precursor in serotonin biosynthesis.
principles.mechanism: Precursor identity for downstream pathways, distinct from circulating supply and brain transport.
principles.scope_limitations: These identities do not establish that additional dietary protein raises brain neurotransmitter synthesis or improves functional or clinical outcomes. Intervention, transport and flux propositions remain Findings requiring separate appraisal.
principles.classification_rationale: Foundational precursor identities are presented as a Principle; historical dietary-effect boundaries remain limitations, not a newly adjudicated negative intervention Finding.
